summary: A target-level plan of finite cyclotomic class groups and their tame characters, cyclic units and capitulation, integral Stickelberger annihilation at every conductor, Herbrand–Ribet, Kummer regularity and units, all prime-power unit indices, cyclotomic growth and Mazur’s inverse-character obstruction. Every prime is included, with dyadic and exceptional-character boundaries explicit. Supplier requests and three precise gaps remain; no formalization claim is made.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic class groups on native carriers
nodes.statement: For every prime p and r≥1, identify A_(p,r)={x∈Cl(O_(K_(p,r))):p^n x=0 for some n} with Cl(O_(K_(p,r)))⊗Z_p. Transport the existing ring-automorphism action, without inversion, along Gal(K_(p,r)/Q)≃(Z/p^r Z)^×. The Artin isomorphism A_(p,r)≃Gal(H_(p,r)/K_(p,r)) is equivariant for conjugation on the right.
hypotheses: K_(p,r)=Q(ζ_(p^r)); H_(p,r) is its maximal everywhere-unramified abelian p-extension; ordinary ideal classes and arithmetic Frobenius are used.
proofSteps: Use finiteness and the primary decomposition of the native class group to compare p-primary torsion with the tensor product.
Restrict ClassGroup.mulEquivHom to p-primary torsion; compute on classes using ClassGroup.mulEquiv_mk0.
Apply global Artin functoriality and normality of the Hilbert class field over Q.
acceptance: On an ideal class, σ sends [a] to [σa]; conjugation sends g to σgσ⁻¹.
At p=2,r=1 the field is Q and A=0.
The comparison commutes with change of primitive root.

sources.match: Normality and Artin equivariance supply the Galois-module comparison.

nodes.title: Teichmüller components at every odd-prime level
nodes.statement: For odd p and r≥1 let Δ_r be the unique subgroup of order p−1 in (Z/p^r Z)^× and Γ_r the kernel of reduction modulo p. Via the Teichmüller lift ω:Δ_r→Z_p^×, define A_(p,r)^(i)=e_i A_(p,r), e_i=(p−1)⁻¹Σ_(a∈Δ_r)ω(a)^(−i)σ_a, for i∈Z/(p−1). This is a Γ_r-stable Z_p-submodule; it is a specialization of the existing character projector, not a new group algebra.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime; r≥1; the action is C0/native-class-action.
proofSteps: Identify the prime-to-p torsion subgroup by Teichmüller lifting.
Specialize the imported character idempotent to ω^i and take its image.
Use commutativity of the cyclotomic Galois group to preserve the wild action.
acceptance: The exponent is −i in the projector and +i in the eigenrelation.
There is no division by the full order p^(r−1)(p−1).

nodes.title: Integral tame decomposition and complex conjugation
nodes.statement: For odd p, A_(p,r) is the direct sum of A_(p,r)^(i) over i∈Z/(p−1), with mutually orthogonal projectors summing to one. Complex conjugation acts on component i by (−1)^i. Norm and extension maps between cyclotomic levels preserve i and satisfy Nj=[K_s:K_r] and jN=Σ Gal(K_s/K_r).
hypotheses: p odd; s≥r≥1; norm and extension are the existing arithmetic maps.
proofSteps: Apply character orthogonality to the tame subgroup and the imported projector evaluation theorem.
Evaluate ω at −1 and use centrality.
Use functoriality of ideal norm/extension and their group-ring norm identities.
acceptance: The decomposition is integral over Z_p, even when p divides the full Galois degree.
The identity jN is a group-ring norm, not multiplication by the degree on arbitrary elements.

nodes.title: Real class groups and the dyadic boundary
nodes.statement: For odd p and r≥1, extension identifies A(K_(p,r)^+) with the c=+1 part of A_(p,r), and the c=−1 part is ker N_(K/K+); the inverse on the plus part is N/2. For p=2 retain ker N, ker(1+c), and A/(1+c)A as distinct native groups, with comparisons whose kernels/cokernels are killed by 2; no integral sign projector is asserted.
hypotheses: K^+ is the native maximal real subfield. At p=2,r=1,2 the real field is Q.
proofSteps: Use Nj=2 and jN=1+c.
Invert 2 only on an odd-primary module to get plus/minus decomposition.
For arbitrary 2-primary modules use (1−c)(1+c)=0 and retain the 2-torsion defects explicitly.
acceptance: Test Z/2 with c=1: it is also killed by 1+c, so a direct sum of signs is invalid.
For odd p, N/2 composed with j and j composed with N/2 are identities on the asserted domains.

nodes.title: The principal prime and the unramified quotient
nodes.statement: For every prime p and r≥1 there is a unique prime P above p in K_(p,r), generated by 1−ζ_(p^r), and its class is zero. Consequently the quotient of the p-Hilbert class group obtained by killing Frobenius at P is canonically A_(p,r) itself. This quotient classifies everywhere-unramified abelian p-extensions in which P splits completely.
proofSteps: Use the cyclotomic integral basis and total ramification formula.
Compute the norm of 1−ζ as Φ_(p^r)(1)=p and identify its prime ideal.
Use the Artin comparison and the splitting condition as quotient by the Frobenius class.
acceptance: Do not quotient out inertia in an already-unramified extension and call that a splitting condition.
The assertion concerns prime-power conductors; it is not an assertion about every prime of every number field.

sources.locator: §1.3, Definition 1.3.19 and Remark 1.3.21, pp.22–23; §3.1, cyclotomic example and Proposition 3.1.11, pp.75–77
sources.match: The S-class quotient kills the prime class; total ramification is combined with the pinned cyclotomic ideal theorem to identify that class as principal.
The unramified quotient and its class-group model are the input to Mazur’s argument.

nodes.title: Hilbert 90 in the cyclic number-field convention
nodes.statement: For a finite cyclic extension L/K with generator σ and x∈L^×, N_(L/K)x=1 iff x=y/σ(y) for some y∈L^×. This is a specialization of the pinned Hilbert 90 theorem. It does not assert y∈O_L^× when x is a unit.
hypotheses: L/K is finite cyclic; the generator is specified.
proofSteps: Apply the existing cyclic Hilbert 90 theorem.
Compute the telescoping norm for the reverse implication.
Keep the distinction between field elements and units in the codomain of the coboundary map.
acceptance: The numerator/denominator agrees with the pinned theorem.
C1/hilbert92 will witness failure of the same statement inside the unit group.

nodes.title: Saturated relative unit lattice
nodes.statement: For a cyclic prime-degree extension L/K, [L:K]=ℓ, let E_K and E_L be full integral unit groups and E_K^sat={u∈E_L:u^n∈E_K for some n≥1}. Define R_(L/K)=E_L/E_K^sat. The norm relation makes it a torsion-free Z[ζ_ℓ]-module with ζ_ℓ acting as σ. A relative fundamental system means lifts of an F_ℓ-basis of R/(1−ζ_ℓ)R.
hypotheses: ℓ is prime; σ generates Gal(L/K); no real place of K becomes complex.
proofSteps: Define saturation inside the existing unit group and quotient by it.
Prove torsion-freeness from full saturation, and show that its prime-to-ℓ torsion enlargement does not change the quotient modulo 1−σ.
Descend σ and the cyclotomic polynomial relation; interpret coinvariants over the Dedekind domain Z[ζ_ℓ].
acceptance: Use the saturation, not the usually torsion-containing quotient E_L/E_K.
No freeness over Z[ζ_ℓ] is inferred from torsion-freeness alone.

sources.match: Hilbert’s relative fundamental units are independence modulo 1−σ after saturation by base-field units.

nodes.title: Hilbert 91: relative fundamental systems
nodes.statement: Under C1/relative-unit-lattice, put d=r₁(K)+r₂(K). Then rank_(Z[ζ_ℓ]) R_(L/K)=d and dim_(F_ℓ) R/(1−ζ_ℓ)R=d. There exist d lifted relative units independent modulo 1−σ in Hilbert’s sense: if ∏H_i^(F_i(σ)) times a saturated base unit lies in (1−σ)E_L, each F_i(ζ_ℓ) is divisible by 1−ζ_ℓ.
hypotheses: Cyclic degree ℓ, prime ℓ; no ramification at infinite places.
proofSteps: Compute the Z-rank by the signatures and Dirichlet’s unit theorem, obtaining d(ℓ−1).
Use the torsion-free cyclotomic-module structure and localization at 1−ζ_ℓ to compute the residue dimension.
Lift a residue basis and translate the relation back to the unit group.
acceptance: Include the independence conclusion and its saturated unit condition.
Do not assert a global Z[ζ_ℓ]-basis.

nodes.title: Hilbert 92 and the unit cohomology count
nodes.statement: For cyclic L/K of prime degree ℓ unramified at infinite places, H¹(G,E_L) has order ℓ·[E_K:N E_L], hence there is a norm-one integral unit that is not y/σ(y) for any integral unit y. The underlying field-element coboundary still exists by Hilbert 90.
hypotheses: Finite cyclic degree ℓ; no infinite-place ramification; E denotes full units.
proofSteps: Import the arithmetic Herbrand quotient q(E_L)=1/ℓ, with q=|H⁰-hat|/|H⁻¹-hat|.
Identify H⁰-hat with E_K/N E_L and H⁻¹-hat with the norm-one units modulo unit coboundaries.
Read off the order and nontriviality.
acceptance: For ℓ=2 the infinite-place hypothesis is retained.
The Herbrand-quotient convention is checked before multiplying by ℓ.

sources.match: There is a norm-one unit not represented by a unit coboundary.
The S-unit Herbrand quotient gives the precise order with the infinite-place factor.

nodes.title: Hilbert 93 and invariant ideals
nodes.statement: For cyclic prime-degree L/K the finite prime divisors of the relative different are exactly the ramified primes; their ramification index is ℓ. More generally, valuation on prime orbits identifies I_L^G/jI_K with ⊕_(finite v of K) Z/e_v Z. In particular this quotient vanishes when the extension is unramified at finite primes.
hypotheses: I is the group of nonzero fractional ideals; G=Gal(L/K); the direct sum has finite support.
proofSteps: Use the existing different/ramification criterion and e_v∈{1,ℓ}.
A G-invariant ideal has constant exponents on each prime orbit, while extension of a base ideal multiplies those exponents by e_v.
Take the orbitwise quotient; do not choose a canonical generator of inertia.
acceptance: The theorem labelled Hilbert 93 includes the different statement itself.
An unramified inert prime contributes zero even when its residue degree is ℓ.

hypotheses: Finite Galois L/K; use the existing class groups and unit cohomology.
proofSteps: Check the ratios are integral units and satisfy the cocycle identity.
Changing α multiplies by a unit coboundary; changing a by a principal ideal gives the same cohomology class.
Use field Hilbert 90 to identify the kernel of the invariant-ideal map.
acceptance: Changing σ to σ⁻¹ changes the representative cocycle compatibly, not the kernel.
The final arrow is not assumed surjective.

The unramified case produces the capitulating ideal class.

nodes.title: Hilbert 94 with its exact kernel size
nodes.statement: If L/K is cyclic of prime degree ℓ and unramified at every finite and infinite place, then #ker(Cl(K)→Cl(L))=ℓ[E_K:N E_L]. The kernel is killed by ℓ, so Cl(K) contains a class of exact order ℓ. This is a capitulation theorem, not a substitute for the general principal ideal theorem.

proofSteps: The invariant-ideal obstruction is zero by Hilbert 93.
Identify the kernel with H¹(G,E_L) and use Hilbert 92’s order formula.
Apply Nj=ℓ to see the kernel is killed by ℓ.

nodes.title: One-prime class-group control
nodes.statement: Let L/K be a finite Galois p-extension, with no ramification at infinite places and at most one ramified finite prime. If Cl(K){p}=0, then Cl(L){p}=0. For a cyclic subextension with exactly one ramified prime, totally ramified, norm induces (Cl(L){p})_G≃Cl(K){p}.
hypotheses: p prime; the first assertion permits a noncyclic finite p-group; the stronger norm assertion assumes cyclicity and total ramification.
proofSteps: Apply the class-field/genus exact sequence to each cyclic prime-degree step.
With at most one inertia group the sum of inertia maps has zero kernel; total ramification also kills its cokernel.
Use the finite p-group Nakayama argument and induction through a central series.
acceptance: Do not infer A_L=0 merely from A_K=0 without the ramification hypothesis.
In the cyclotomic tower the prime above p is totally ramified at every nontrivial step.

proofSteps: Form the finite rational linear combination in the existing group algebra.
Compare the sum indexed by units modulo m with the sum over integers prime to m.
Check independence under a simultaneous change of the cyclotomic field model and primitive root.

nodes.title: Gauss-sum principal ideal factorization
nodes.statement: Let ℓ≡1 mod m be prime, l a prime of Q(ζ_m) over ℓ, and choose a primitive root c modulo ℓ and χ(c)=ζ_m with ζ_m mod l=c^(−(ℓ−1)/m). For g=−Σ_(x∈F_ℓ^×)χ(x)ζ_ℓ^x, in K(ζ_ℓ) the normalized valuations at σ_b⁻¹L are (ℓ−1){b/m}; equivalently (g^(ℓ−1))=l^((ℓ−1)θ_m) as fractional ideals of K. For x∈J_m, g^x lies in K^× and (g^x)=l^(xθ_m).
hypotheses: m≥2; ℓ∤m; the auxiliary character/root compatibility is imposed as written; L is the unique prime above l.
proofSteps: Compare the negative Gauss-sum convention with the pinned positive gaussSum; multiplying by −1 does not change its ideal.
Use the nontrivial-character product formula g(χ)g(χ⁻¹)=χ(−1)ℓ to bound valuations.
Compare the tame inertia action on g and the uniformizer ζ_ℓ−1 to identify valuations modulo ℓ−1 and hence exactly.
Use the smoothing generators to descend g^x to K, then cancel the common exponent ℓ−1 in the free fractional-ideal group.
acceptance: If an arbitrary c is used, record the extra unit index a and the translated θ_m instead of silently setting a=1.
The product formula requires nontrivial χ, including the m=2 boundary.

sources.locator: §4.5, Lemma 4.5.4, p.115, and proof of Theorem 4.5.6, pp.115–117
sources.match: Descent of smoothed Gauss sums and their valuations prove the principal ideal identity; use the corrected Gauss product recorded in E2.

nodes.title: Stickelberger annihilation of the full class group
nodes.statement: For every m≥2, the integral ideal I_m annihilates the full ideal class group of Q(ζ_m), hence all of its primary parts. In particular s_(m,b)·[a]=0 for every ideal class and every positive b prime to m.
hypotheses: All conductors m≥2; no odd-prime restriction.
proofSteps: Use Chebotarev in the Galois Hilbert class field to represent any ideal class by a prime over a rational prime completely split in K.
Apply the smoothed Gauss-sum principal ideal identity to that representative.
Use the generating description of I_m to obtain annihilation for every element.
acceptance: Annihilation is integral; θ_m alone is not asserted to act on an arbitrary finite class group.
Both m=2 and composite m are included.

sources.match: The integral Stickelberger ideal annihilates every ideal class.

nodes.title: Bernoulli character evaluation and Kummer congruence
nodes.statement: For odd prime p and nontrivial tame χ define the notation B_(1,χ)=p⁻¹Σ_(a=1)^(p−1)aχ(a) in a p-adic coefficient field. Then ω^i(θ_p)=B_(1,ω^(−i)). For even 2≤k≤p−3, B_(1,ω^(k−1)) belongs to Z_p and B_(1,ω^(k−1))≡B_k/k mod p. Here B₁=−1/2 and rational divisibility always means numerator divisibility.
hypotheses: The finite sum is a notation for the existing generalized Bernoulli value; χ is extended by zero on multiples of p.
proofSteps: Evaluate the finite group-ring sum with the inverse basis convention.
Replace Teichmüller representatives modulo p² by a^(p) and apply the power-sum congruence.
Apply the classical Kummer congruence to reduce the resulting Bernoulli index; keep the exceptional pole at i=1 separate.
acceptance: For p=5,k=2 the residue is 1/12≡3 mod5.
The character for B_k is ω^(k−1), so its class-group component is ω^(1−k).

sources.locator: I §2, power-sum and Kummer congruences, pp.52–54; proof of Corollary 2.9
sources.match: The character sum is compared modulo p with the appropriate ordinary Bernoulli value.
The finite character sum evaluates θ.

nodes.title: Projected annihilators and the exceptional character
nodes.statement: For odd p and odd i≢1 mod p−1, B_(1,ω^(−i))∈Z_p annihilates A_(p,1)^(i). In component i=1 the smoothing b=1+p has scalar pB_(1,ω⁻¹), a p-adic unit; therefore A_(p,1)^(1)=0. The unsmoothed B_(1,ω⁻¹) is not declared integral.
hypotheses: Odd i is a residue class modulo p−1; for the nonexceptional case choose b with ω(b)^i−b a unit.
proofSteps: Project the integral smoothings using C0/decomposition.
For i≠1 choose a residue unit separating ω^i from ω.
For i=1 use b=1+p; the reduced sum Σaω(a)⁻¹ is p−1≡−1 modp.
acceptance: For the positive smoothing b−σ_b at b=1+p, the scalar pB_(1,ω⁻¹) reduces to −1 modulo p. Reversing the smoothing reverses this unit sign.
This vanishing is for ω, and must not be substituted for the different assertion about ω⁻¹.

sources.match: Integral smoothing gives the Bernoulli annihilator and the exceptional-character vanishing.
The integral annihilator is stated separately from the exceptional component.

nodes.title: Herbrand’s theorem
nodes.statement: For every odd prime p and even k with 2≤k≤p−3, A_(p,1)^(1−k)≠0 implies p divides the numerator of B_k. Equivalently, if that numerator is prime to p, the component vanishes.
hypotheses: No bound on p other than primality and oddness; the k interval is empty at p=3.
proofSteps: Apply the projected Bernoulli annihilator in character i=1−k.
Use C3/bernoulli-comparison to identify its residue with B_k/k.
A p-adic unit acts invertibly on a finite p-primary module, so a nonzero component forces the residue to vanish.
acceptance: Use A^(1−k), not A^(k−1).
The assertion is nonvanishing, not an equality of lengths with a Bernoulli valuation.

sources.match: Nonvanishing forces Bernoulli divisibility with the inverse-character indexing.
The older direction is Herbrand’s theorem.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic reflection and the two exceptional components
nodes.statement: For every odd prime p and even residue k modulo p−1, r_p(A_(p,1)^(k))≤r_p(A_(p,1)^(1−k))≤r_p(A_(p,1)^(k))+1. Also A_(p,1)^(0)=A_(p,1)^(1)=0; at k=0 the sharper equality of ranks is zero on both sides. Here r_p(M)=dim_(F_p)(M/pM).
hypotheses: Use full integral units, their p-th-power quotient, and the natural Δ action.
proofSteps: Apply Kummer duality to the radical of everywhere-unramified p-extensions and compare its ideal valuation sequence with units modulo p-th powers.
The duality with μ_p sends character i to 1−i; the even nontrivial unit character has rank one by Dirichlet’s theorem.
The trivial class component is the p-part of Cl(Q), hence zero; the exceptional radical Q(μ_(p²))/Q(μ_p) is ramified, eliminating its defect.
Combine the rank inequalities and use Nakayama for finite p-groups.
acceptance: The Kummer dual uses 1−i, whereas the constant-coefficient dual in C8 uses −i.
Do not claim equality of ranks in every nontrivial character.

sources.match: Reflection compares complementary characters through the Kummer pairing and the unit contribution.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic class-number and regulator comparisons
nodes.statement: For every CM abelian field F, write X(F) for its primitive Dirichlet characters, E_F for full units and R_F^+=R_(F+). Then h_F^−=2[E_F:E_(F+)]∏_(χ odd)(−B_(1,χ)/2), and h_F^+R_F^+=∏_(χ even,χ≠1)(−(1/2)Σ_(a=1)^(fχ)χ(a)log|1−exp(2πia/fχ)|). At prime-power cyclotomic conductor Q_F=[E_F:μ(F)E_(F+)]=1; at conductor two use Q directly. These are comparisons with native class numbers and regulators, not new analytic objects.
hypotheses: F is CM and abelian over Q; the product uses primitive conductors fχ, even if the ambient cyclotomic conductor is larger.
proofSteps: Factor the native Dedekind zeta Euler product into the primitive character L-functions using the Frobenius/splitting dictionary, then use continuation.
Apply the pinned analytic class-number residue theorem to F and F+.
Use the primitive-character values at zero and one, the conductor-discriminant formula and the product of Gauss sums; the precise L-value and conductor contracts are requested.
Compare CM and real regulators through the full unit index, retaining roots of unity and the factor 2 at every step.
acceptance: For Q(ζ₃), the relative formula gives h^−=1 using [μ₆:{±1}]=3 and B_(1,χ)=−1/3.
Never multiply imprimitive L-values at an ambient level without their Euler-factor correction.
The native residue theorem is already in Mathlib and receives no new theorem node.

sources.locator: §4.1, Proposition 4.1.21, p.100; §4.2, Theorem 4.2.14, Corollary 4.2.15, Lemmas 4.2.16–4.2.19 and Theorem 4.2.20, pp.104–108
sources.match: The primitive-character product and regulator comparisons give both class-number formulas.

nodes.title: Relative class-number bound for the modular construction
nodes.statement: For every odd prime p, h_p^−=h(Q(ζ_p))/h(Q(ζ_p)^+) satisfies h_p^−<p^((p−1)/4). Consequently the number t of even k∈[2,p−3] with p dividing numerator(B_k) is less than (p−1)/4.
hypotheses: h_p^− is the positive integer relative class number, not the order of an integral negative eigenspace at p=2.
proofSteps: Use the cyclotomic relative class-number product and its Maillet determinant expression.
Apply Hadamard to the determinant to obtain h_p^−≤p^((p+3)/4)2^(−(p−1)/4), sufficient for p>19.
For p≤19 compute the finite relative class-number products to get h_p^−=1.
Each irregular even index contributes at least one factor of p to the relative class-number product, giving p^t≤h_p^−.
acceptance: This counts indices, not their Bernoulli valuations.
Read the Maillet determinant identity before treating the bound as source-closed; the precise source gap is recorded.

sources.match: The class-number bound and the count of irregular indices produce a weight-two unit-constant form.
The product formula relates the relative class number to odd character values.

nodes.title: The weight-two Eisenstein congruence
nodes.statement: For odd p and even 2≤k≤p−3 with p|num(B_k), there exist a finite coefficient field E, a prime λ|p and a normalized cuspidal eigen-newform f of weight 2, level p and nebentypus ε=ω^(k−2), with λ-integral coefficients and a_ℓ(f)≡1+ℓ^(k−1) modλ for every prime ℓ≠p. The chosen p-adic embedding defines ε, and ε modλ=χ_p^(k−2).
hypotheses: All irregular pairs in the stated range; k=2 is impossible because B₂=1/6.
proofSteps: Use G_(2,ε) with constant L(−1,ε)/2 and nonconstant divisor-sum coefficients; prove its coefficient and constant-term congruence with E_k using the Bernoulli congruence.
Construct an integral weight-two form with unit constant term using Ribet’s weight-one Eisenstein products and the strict irregular-index bound.
Subtract the constant term times this auxiliary form to obtain a semi-cusp congruent to the Eisenstein series.
Apply the integral Hecke eigenlifting lemma and the newform decomposition, preserving the good-prime congruence and nontrivial nebentypus.
acceptance: A congruence of positive q-coefficients alone is insufficient: the constant term and integrality must be proved.
Generic Eisenstein series, eigenlifting and Hecke theory remain supplier contracts.

sources.locator: §3, Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.3, Propositions 3.4–3.6 and Theorem 3.7, pp.155–159
sources.match: The modular construction changes weight to two while preserving the required residual eigenvalues.

nodes.title: The nonsplit residual extension
nodes.statement: For an irregular pair (p,k), construct a finite field F of characteristic p and a continuous representation ρ:G_Q→GL₂(F) fitting into a nonsplit extension 0→F→V→F(χ_p^(k−1))→0, unramified outside p. It is obtained from a stable lattice in the absolutely irreducible weight-two newform representation, with arithmetic Frobenius traces a_ℓ and determinants ε(ℓ)ℓ.
hypotheses: p odd; k even, 2≤k≤p−3; p|num(B_k); χ_p is the mod-p cyclotomic character.
proofSteps: Import the characteristic-zero newform representation and absolute irreducibility.
Use the Eisenstein congruence, Chebotarev and lattice independence to identify the residual semisimplification as 1⊕χ_p^(k−1).
Apply the imported Ribet lattice theorem in the orientation with trivial subline.
Retain unramifiedness outside p and continuity on the finite image.
acceptance: The representation is globally nonsplit, not just reducible.
Reversing subline and quotient reverses the final character.

sources.match: Lattice choice turns residual reducibility into the required nonsplit oriented extension.

nodes.title: The local finite-flat splitting at p
nodes.statement: The representation of C4/residual-extension can be chosen so that the image of a decomposition group at p has order prime to p. Over the completion of Q(ζ_p)^+ it is the generic fibre of a finite flat F-vector group scheme; the trivial subline extends to a constant étale subgroup, its complementary quotient is connected, and the connected–étale decomposition splits the local extension.
hypotheses: The base local extension has absolute ramification index e=(p−1)/2<p−1; the irregular-pair hypotheses remain.
proofSteps: Realize the weight-two representation on the Tate module of the modular quotient A_f of J₁(p)/J₀(p).
Use the Deligne–Rapoport good-reduction theorem over Q(ζ_p)^+ to produce the finite flat torsion model, with closure and quotient retaining the F action.
Apply Raynaud uniqueness at e<p−1 to identify the closure of the trivial line with its constant model.
The determinant character is ramified and the other rank-one factor has connected special fibre; apply the connected–étale result to split the opposite-order extension.
Descend the prime-to-p image property from the base of degree prime to p.
acceptance: Retain the ramification-index bound; finite flatness by itself does not imply splitting.
The good-reduction assertion is a precise requested supplier extension, not a consequence of the word semistable.

sources.match: Good reduction over the real cyclotomic local field and small ramification force local splitting.

nodes.title: Ribet’s unramified elementary abelian extension
nodes.statement: Construct E/Q finite Galois containing K=Q(ζ_p), such that H=Gal(E/K) is a nonzero elementary abelian p-group, E/K is unramified at every place, and Δ acts on H by ω^(1−k). E is the compositum of K with the fixed field of the kernel of the finite residual representation; the latter field alone need not contain K.
hypotheses: p odd and k an irregular even index in [2,p−3].
proofSteps: Take the compositum with K so that every diagonal cyclotomic character is trivial over the base. The restricted image of G_K is an additive subgroup of F.
If that image were zero the global extension would factor through Δ of order prime to p and split, contradicting nonsplitting.
Away from p use residual unramifiedness; at p the image is both a p-group and of order prime to p, hence trivial.
Conjugation of the upper-right entry by diag(1,χ_p^(k−1)) gives χ_p^(1−k); CM eliminates infinite ramification.
acceptance: The extension is nontrivial over K, not merely over Q.
It is unramified also at p; removing p from the condition would not prove Ribet.

sources.locator: §1, Theorems 1.2–1.3, p.152; completion of the proof in §4, p.162
sources.match: The finite residual image gives the unramified extension with the complementary character.

Provides the comparison between residual extension characters and class groups.

nodes.title: Ribet’s converse and the Herbrand–Ribet equivalence
nodes.statement: For every odd prime p and even 2≤k≤p−3, p|num(B_k) iff A_(p,1)^(1−k)≠0 iff (A_(p,1)/pA_(p,1))^(1−k)≠0. The converse follows from Ribet’s modular construction, independently of the cyclotomic main conjecture.
hypotheses: Class groups have the covariant Galois action of C0.
proofSteps: Apply Artin reciprocity to the nonzero unramified character quotient in C4/unramified-extension.
Use the exact tame projector and finite-module Nakayama to pass between A and A/p.
Combine with Herbrand’s implication.
acceptance: At (p,k)=(37,32) the component index is 5.
The equivalence asserts existence, not cyclicity, cardinality, or equality of Fitting ideals.

sources.match: Ribet proves Bernoulli divisibility gives a nonzero complementary class-group component.

nodes.title: Regular primes
nodes.statement: For a prime p define IsRegularPrime(p) to mean p does not divide h(Q(ζ_p)), equivalently A_(p,1)=0. The predicate is stated for every prime, including p=2, where K=Q and regularity holds.
hypotheses: p prime; class number is the native positive finite cardinality.
proofSteps: Use NumberField.classNumber and divisibility of a natural number.
Compare with the finite p-primary subgroup using primary decomposition.
acceptance: The convention includes the rational conductor-two case.

sources.match: Regularity is class-number indivisibility.
Regularity propagates up the cyclotomic p-tower.

api.statement: Regularity is exactly p∤h(Q(ζ_p)).

api.name: isRegularPrime_primary
api.statement: Regularity is equivalent to A_(p,1)=0.

api.statement: Regularity is unchanged by replacing the cyclotomic field with an isomorphic model.

tests.statement: p=2 is regular because Q(ζ₂)=Q has class number one.

tests.statement: Vanishing of the real p-class group alone is the Vandiver predicate, not this definition.

uses.how: Identifies the computable Bernoulli test.
Rules out an everywhere-unramified radical extension.
Propagates the class-group vanishing.

nodes.title: Kummer’s criterion for regularity
nodes.statement: For every odd prime p, IsRegularPrime(p) iff p divides none of the numerators B₂,B₄,…,B_(p−3). Together with the direct p=2 case this covers every prime.
hypotheses: The list is empty for p=3; Bernoulli convention B₁=−1/2.
proofSteps: Regularity kills every tame component, so Herbrand–Ribet excludes irregular indices.
Conversely the Bernoulli condition kills all nonexceptional odd components by Herbrand; the exceptional odd component is zero by C3/projected-annihilator.
Reflection kills every even component, including the trivial one; sum the projectors.
acceptance: The proof accounts for even components, rather than identifying total and relative class numbers without argument.
The Bernoulli denominator is never used as a numerator.

sources.locator: Introduction, p.151, discussion of Kummer’s theorem and Theorem 1.1
sources.match: The full regular-prime criterion is refined by the characterwise equivalence.
Reflection supplies the even components that the odd Bernoulli criterion must also control.

nodes.title: Unramified extensions from primary units
nodes.statement: For odd p and K=Q(ζ_p), if v∈O_K^× and v≡1 modλ^p with λ=1−ζ_p, then K(v^(1/p))/K is unramified at every finite place; it is either trivial or cyclic of degree p. This is the primary-unit local criterion, with the higher exponent p essential.
hypotheses: K contains μ_p; λ denotes both the element and its principal prime as appropriate.
proofSteps: Away from p the radicand is a unit and p is invertible, so the Kummer extension is unramified.
At λ use Hilbert’s local calculation: after subtracting a p-th power, the integral generator and its minimal equation have unit discriminant in the unramified case, including the trivial extension.
Use Kummer theory to identify the possible degree and cyclic group.
acceptance: Congruence merely modulo λ is not enough.
The trivial radical case is included, so a degree-p conclusion needs a non-p-th-power hypothesis.

sources.match: The local primary-radical calculation controls the discriminant.
The λ^p-congruent unit gives an unramified radical extension.

nodes.title: Kummer’s lemma for regular primes
nodes.statement: For every odd regular prime p and unit u∈O_(Q(ζ_p))^×, if u is congruent to an integer modulo pO_K, then u=v^p for some v∈O_K^×.
hypotheses: The congruence is modulo pO_K, not modulo λ.
proofSteps: For a generator σ of Δ, form w=u/σ(u). Since u is integer-congruent modulo p, w≡1 modλ^p.
If w is not a p-th power, the primary-radical criterion gives an everywhere-unramified cyclic degree-p extension, contradicting Hilbert 94 and regularity.

On E_K/E_K^p the Δ-norm of u is zero: its rational norm is ±1 and odd p makes these p-th powers. Because p∤|Δ|, σ−1 is invertible on this augmentation subspace. Thus w being a p-th power implies u is one.
A p-th root in K of a unit is integral and invertible, by its valuations.
acceptance: Do not infer the original u-radical is unramified without the primary calculation for u/σu.
For p=3, ζ₃≡1 modλ but is not a cube of a global unit, detecting the wrong modulus.

sources.locator: §141, Satz 156, pp.437–440, especially the second proof on p.440
sources.match: Hilbert proves Kummer’s unit lemma through the unramified radical extension.
The unit conclusion and the congruence modulo p are stated explicitly.

nodes.title: Regularity at every prime-power level
nodes.statement: If p is an odd regular prime then A_(p,r)=0 and p∤h(K_(p,r)) for every r≥1. Norm and extension comparisons and every tame eigenspace therefore vanish at all these levels.
hypotheses: No restriction on r other than r≥1.
proofSteps: Each successive cyclotomic step has degree p and exactly one ramified finite prime, totally ramified.
The fields are CM, so there is no infinite-place ramification.
Iterate C1/one-prime-control from the regular base.
acceptance: The statement covers p^r conductors, not just p.
At an irregular prime no higher-level vanishing is inferred.

sources.match: Regularity at the first level forces vanishing throughout the cyclotomic tower.

nodes.title: Odd class numbers throughout the dyadic tower
nodes.statement: For every r≥1, the class number of Q(ζ_(2^r)) is odd, so its 2-primary class group is zero. In particular the real subfield also has odd class number.
hypotheses: The first field is Q; the next is Q(i).
proofSteps: Use h(Q)=h(Q(i))=1, with the latter given by the Gaussian Euclidean domain or the native Minkowski bound.
Starting at Q(i), successive quadratic steps have only the prime over 2 ramified and no real places.
Apply one-prime control at every step; descend to the real subfield by the norm-surjectivity class-field argument, not by dividing 2.
acceptance: The real-to-complex first step is handled separately; Hilbert 94 without the infinite-place condition is not used.
No integral plus/minus projector at 2 occurs.

sources.match: One-prime propagation applies once the dyadic tower is based at Q(i).

nodes.title: Cyclotomic units at every prime-power conductor
nodes.statement: For every prime p and r≥1, inside K_(p,r)^× let D_(p,r) be generated by μ(K_(p,r)) and the nonzero elements 1−ζ_(p^r)^a with 1≤a<p^r. Define C_(p,r)=D_(p,r)∩O_K^× and C_(p,r)^+=C_(p,r)∩(K^+)^×. Thus circular numbers are formed in the field before intersecting with integral units. At conductor 2 include −1 explicitly through μ(Q).
hypotheses: Use the native field, unit subgroup and maximal real subfield. This finite-level definition is relocated from IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/cyclotomic-unit-group, which must import it.
proofSteps: Generate a multiplicative subgroup in K^×, then take the preimage along O_K^×→K^×.
Use valuations at the unique prime over p to recognize products that are units.
Intersect with the real field and retain all torsion, including signs.
acceptance: The nonunit 1−ζ_(p^r) belongs to D, but not to C.
No subgroup of integral units is generated directly by nonunits.

sources.match: Cyclotomic units are the integral-unit intersection of circular numbers; the explicit torsion convention fixes conductor two.

nodes.title: Real generators and the full-to-real unit quotient
nodes.statement: For m=p^r, r≥1, C is generated by μ(K) and the ratios η_a=(1−ζ_m^a)/(1−ζ_m), (a,p)=1. The real subgroup is generated by −1 and ζ_m^tη_a with 2t≡1−a mod m when p is odd; at p=2 use odd integer a and t=(1−a)/2. Except the rational small-conductor boundaries, the Hasse unit index is one: O_K^×=μ(K)O_(K+)^× and C=μ(K)C^+, giving a canonical isomorphism O_(K+)^×/C^+≃O_K^×/C.
hypotheses: All prime powers; conductor 2 is handled as Q, and conductor 4 has real field Q. Relocates IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/smoothed-cyclotomic-unit, cyclotomic-unit-generators and unit-index-real-full.
proofSteps: Use distribution relations to reduce lower-conductor circular numbers to the ratios at the top conductor.
Correct each ratio by the stated root of unity so complex conjugation fixes it.
Use the prime-power Hasse unit-index argument: a unit divided by its conjugate is a root of unity, and reduction at the unique ramified prime eliminates the extra index.
Identify the kernel of the inclusion of real units in the full quotient as exactly C^+.
acceptance: At conductor 8,a=3 the correction is ζ₈⁻¹; there is no inverse of 2 modulo 8.
The quotient isomorphism is between unit quotients, not a claimed isomorphism to an ideal class group.

nodes.title: The prime-power cyclotomic unit index theorem
nodes.statement: For every prime p and r≥1, [O_(K_(p,r)^+)^×:C_(p,r)^+]=[O_(K_(p,r))^×:C_(p,r)]=h(K_(p,r)^+). The indices are finite and computed before removing torsion. The p-primary part of either unit quotient has cardinality equal to #A(K_(p,r)^+).
hypotheses: Includes p=2 and the rational boundary r=1. Relocates IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/index-formula and dyadic-prime-power-index.
proofSteps: Compute the regulator of the real generator lattice by the finite abelian group determinant identity.
Compare the product of its nontrivial even-character logarithmic sums with the real analytic class-number formula, including conductor reduction for imprimitive characters.
Divide by the full real regulator to obtain the index; use C6/unit-generators for the full-unit quotient.
For dyadic conductor use the odd-a generators and the same real regulator argument; treat Q and Q(i) directly.
acceptance: No canonical isomorphism C-quotient≃Cl(K^+) follows from equality of cardinalities.
At conductor 8 both indices are one, agreeing with C5/dyadic-tower.

sources.match: The odd-prime theorem is proved by an exact regulator comparison; its dyadic adaptation requires the explicit supplier contract recorded below.

nodes.title: The Kummer–Vandiver statement
nodes.statement: For every prime p let VandiverAt(p) mean p∤h(Q(ζ_p)^+). The Kummer–Vandiver conjecture is the assertion that VandiverAt(p) holds for every odd prime p. This roadmap defines and compares the assertion and never supplies a theorem or an axiom asserting it for all primes.
hypotheses: K^+ is the native maximal real subfield, not an arbitrary chosen totally real field.
proofSteps: Define the per-prime divisibility predicate on NumberField.classNumber.
State the universal odd-prime assertion as a mathematical conjecture only.
Separate it from total-field regularity through the norm/extension comparison.
acceptance: There is no universal Vandiver theorem target.
The conjecture is not used to prove any preceding or following theorem.

sources.match: The real class number and even components specify precisely the plus-part assertion; this does not prove its universal nondivisibility.
Vandiver is the vanishing conjecture for the even class-group components.

nodes.title: Vandiver comparisons and the regular-prime implication
nodes.statement: For odd prime p, VandiverAt(p) iff A(K_(p,1)^+)=0 iff all even components A_(p,1)^(i) vanish iff the p-primary part of the real cyclotomic-unit quotient vanishes. IsRegularPrime(p) implies VandiverAt(p). Neither VandiverAt(p) nor its negation is assumed universally.
hypotheses: Only prime-level equivalences are asserted; arbitrary-level unit-index comparisons remain C6/unit-index.
proofSteps: Apply the odd-primary real transfer comparison.
Use the even/odd character decomposition.
Use the exact index theorem and primary decomposition of the finite unit quotient.
A zero total p-class group has zero plus part.

Regularity is a sufficient condition, rather than a redefinition of Vandiver.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic tower normalization
nodes.statement: For odd p use F_n=Q(ζ_(p^(n+1))), n≥0, over F₀=Q(ζ_p); for p=2 use F_n=Q(ζ_(2^(n+2))) over F₀=Q(i). These are Z_p-towers with [F_n:F₀]=p^n and a unique totally ramified prime above p. The conductor-two field Q is kept separately. The finite A_n and norm maps are exactly the native class modules and maps imported from IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.2/class-group-limit.
hypotheses: Fix compatible primitive roots; tame Δ acts only for odd p.
proofSteps: Use the cyclotomic Galois equivalence and the odd-p Teichmüller/wild decomposition.
At p=2 remove the sign factor by starting at conductor 4.
Transport the imported class-group inverse system along these field identifications and preserve norms.
acceptance: The base conductor for p=2 is 4, never 2 if the layer degrees are to equal 2^n.
Do not form the inverse limit using extension maps.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic Artin comparison and exact control
nodes.statement: For the towers of C7/cyclotomic-tower, X=lim_N A_n is the imported compact unramified Iwasawa module and canonically Gal(H_∞/F_∞). For every n≥0, norm gives X/(γ^(p^n)−1)X≃A_n. For odd p this is Δ-equivariant and decomposes into the finite tame components. At p=2 the same assertion uses the whole module without sign projectors.
hypotheses: H_∞ is the maximal everywhere-unramified abelian pro-p extension of F_∞; γ is a topological generator of Γ.
proofSteps: Apply the imported inverse-limit Artin comparison.
In the class-field inertia control sequence there is one inertia summand and its map to Γ^(p^n) is an isomorphism by total ramification; both control defects vanish.
Use the central tame action to commute projections with the compact inverse limit.
acceptance: Exact control is proved from the one-prime hypothesis and is not asserted for every Z_p-extension.
Norm maps between the finite p-class groups are surjective in these towers.

nodes.title: Iwasawa growth of cyclotomic class numbers
nodes.statement: For every prime p the tower F_n of C7/cyclotomic-tower has invariants μ,λ∈N, ν∈Z and n₀ such that v_p(h(F_n))=μp^n+λn+ν for every n≥n₀. μ and λ are the imported invariants of X over Z_p[[Γ]] and are independent of γ. At p=2, μ=λ=ν=0 works for every n; the same holds for odd regular p.
hypotheses: Use the n-indexing fixed in C7/cyclotomic-tower; ν may be negative for a general tower.
proofSteps: Apply the general arithmetic class-number growth theorem of IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2, whose full generality is every Z_p-extension, to these towers.
Use C7/cyclotomic-control to compare its X and finite class groups with the present conventions.
For the dyadic and regular cases use the finite-level vanishing to identify X=0 and all valuations as zero.
acceptance: The growth law is eventual; n₀ is part of the conclusion.
No equality μ=0 for all odd p is asserted here; Ferrero–Washington remains with its owner.
Replacing the base by F_s changes μ to p^sμ and ν to ν+sλ in the reindexed formula.

sources.match: The finite torsion Iwasawa module gives the eventual μp^n+λn+ν growth law.

nodes.title: Mazur’s inverse-character vanishing
nodes.statement: For every odd prime p and every r≥1, A_(p,r)^(−1)=0. More generally, for j∈{1,3,5,7,9}, A_(p,r)^(−j)=0 for every odd prime p and every r≥1, and A_(p,r)^(−11)=0 for every r≥1 when p≠691. For p=2 the whole A_(2,r) is zero for every r≥1. Characters are reduced modulo p−1, including the exceptional ω case.
hypotheses: χ_P in Mazur’s notation is the Teichmüller character ω, not an arbitrary odd character.
proofSteps: Use the projected annihilator and reduce −j modulo p−1.
For a nonexceptional character, Kummer’s congruence reduces its Bernoulli scalar to B_(j+1)/(j+1), with the p-denominator boundary treated by the exceptional smoothing.

Use B₂=1/6, B₄=−1/30, B₆=1/42, B₈=−1/30, B₁₀=5/66. Reduce the exponent before using a Bernoulli congruence at small p; for p=5 and j=9 the component has index 3 and is controlled by B₂, not by the numerator 5 in B₁₀.
For j=11 use B₁₂=−691/2730 and retain the prime 691.

For each odd-prime character i, exact control gives X^(i)/(γ−1)X^(i)≃A_(p,1)^(i). The imported finite generation and compact Nakayama imply X^(i)=0 when this base component vanishes; control then gives A_(p,r)^(i)=0 at every r. Use the dyadic theorem for p=2.
acceptance: At p=691 the exponent −11 is the irregular B₁₂ component, so a universal vanishing assertion would contradict Herbrand–Ribet.
Higher-level vanishing requires the exact-control and compact-Nakayama step; a conductor-p citation alone does not prove it.

sources.match: The inverse low odd characters vanish, with the Bernoulli-numerator exception at 691.
Finite generation and exact one-prime control propagate a zero tame base component to the full cyclotomic tower by compact Nakayama.

nodes.title: The unramified inverse-character quotient
nodes.statement: Let p be any odd prime, r≥1, K=K_(p,r), and E/K an everywhere-unramified abelian p-extension stable over Q. If conjugation by Δ_r on H=Gal(E/K) is scalar ω⁻¹, then H=0 and E=K, without any assumption that the wild action is trivial. The same conclusion holds for any ω⁻¹ quotient of the p-Hilbert group with the prime above p required to split, since that splitting quotient is canonically A_(p,r). At p=2 every everywhere-unramified abelian 2-extension of K_(2,r) is trivial.
hypotheses: The scalar character condition is on H itself, not on its constant-coefficient dual; E/K is unramified at p as well as elsewhere.
proofSteps: Use the equivariant Artin surjection A_(p,r)→H at the specified level.
Project to exponent −1 using the exact tame decomposition.
Apply C8/mazur-odd-vanishing; use C0/prime-above-p for the extra splitting condition.
acceptance: A p-ramified extension does not satisfy this theorem.
This is the precise class-field obstruction needed by the Eisenstein-ideal consumer.

sources.locator: I §2, pp.50–54, especially Proposition 2.8 and Corollary 2.10
sources.match: The class-group vanishing removes the relevant unramified quotient.
The higher-level consequence uses the exact-control propagation in C8/mazur-odd-vanishing.

nodes.title: Constant-coefficient étale cohomology and inverse characters
nodes.statement: For odd p and every r≥1, put K=K_(p,r). Identify H¹_et(Spec O_K,F_p) with Hom_(F_p)(A_(p,r)/p,F_p), equivariantly for the pullback/conjugation convention. Its tame character-j component is dual to the character-(−j) part of A_(p,r)/p, retaining the contragredient wild action. In particular H¹_et(Spec O_K,F_p)^(1)=0. The algebraic dual Hom_(F_p)(A_(p,r)/p,μ_p(K)) has instead the character shift i↦1−i; this is a twisted class-group dual, not an assertion that μ_p is an étale group scheme over O_K. For p=2 the constant-coefficient group is zero at every r.
hypotheses: The coefficient F_p is constant with trivial Δ action; ordinary everywhere-unramified abelian p-extensions are used.
proofSteps: Apply the étale fundamental group and class-field comparison to constant torsors.
Compute (σf)(x)=f(σ⁻¹x), which inverts the character.
Tensor the constant-valued class-group dual with μ_p(K) to obtain the ω twist. Apply the all-level inverse-character vanishing; treat p=2 through the zero dyadic class group.
acceptance: The component that vanishes on constant H¹ is +1, corresponding to class exponent −1.
The twisted class-group dual and constant étale H¹ have different tame character shifts; μ_p over O_K is not used as an étale coefficient group scheme.

sources.match: The étale character components are related to unramified class-field quotients.
The character on a Hom space is the quotient of the target and source characters.
